title: SLA-driven kernel fallback thresholds and regional failover to recover tokens/sec cliff
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customer escalation: multiple enterprise customers reported sudden tokens/sec collapse (70% drop) and extended first-byte delays after last night’s model variant refresh. Impact spans Hosted API, Dedicated pools in us-west-2, and one Private VPC deployment (AcmeRetail). Root cause appears to be a combination of an updated model artifact (quantized-int8 variant) + a new kernel selection heuristic that caused repeated kernel rebinds and KV-cache fragmentation on long-context requests (~4k). This ticket tracks the urgent production bugfix (short-term mitigations + medium-term safeguards) to restore SLA and prevent recurrence.
updates: 2026-03-10 01:22 UTC - Incident opened by CSM after customer report (AcmeRetail). Pager alerted core infra team. Initial symptoms: sustained token/sec drop and elevated TTFT across affected clusters.

2026-03-10 02:05 UTC - Mitigation 1: Rollback model variant rollout in hosted canary and paused pipeline for dedicated auto-rollouts. Observed ~30% recovery but instability persisted in some Dedicated pools and one Private deployment.

2026-03-10 03:40 UTC - Investigation: Profiling traces show frequent kernel re-selection (kernel hysteresis) when scheduler encountered mixed quantized/dense operator paths. This caused KV cache evictions and increased priming work for long contexts. See trace: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/trace/TTFT-557001

2026-03-10 04:12 UTC - Hotpatch applied: Introduced conservative kernel-fallback threshold (disable aggressive quant->dense swap for requests >2048 tokens). Patch deployed to hosted and Dedicated us-west-2 via rolling restart. Private deployment owner (AcmeRetail) coordinated manual patch application.

2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Outcome: Tokens/sec returned to 95% of baseline for hosted and dedicated after fallback threshold; Private deployment recovered after manual kernel threshold change and restart. Full SLA restoration pending validation for multi-model fanout traffic.

2026-03-12 14:30 UTC - Post-mortem analysis started. Hypothesis: nightly model refresh introduced new weight layout that interacts poorly with kernel selector's latency vs memory heuristic under specific sequence length distributions.

2026-03-13 11:15 UTC - Engineering decision: ship adaptive hysteresis with metrics-driven backoff (experiment A) and add a regional failover policy that routes heavy long-context traffic to variants with stable kernel paths. Filed design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Kernel+Fallback+Policy

2026-03-13 15:42 UTC - PR: runtime patch (conservative-fallback) opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345. Code owners: @liamorourke @sachin. Requesting expedited review and canary merge.

2026-03-14 07:00 UTC - Observability: New Grafana alerts created for sustained token/sec drop (>20% below baseline for 10m) and kernel-rebind-rate (>5 rebinds/min). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttft/throughput-cliff

2026-03-14 09:05 UTC - Blocker: Private deployment automation doesn't currently support kernel-threshold toggles via control plane; scheduler change required. Follow-up ticket planned for private agent upgrade path.
2026-03-14 12:50 UTC - Customer comms: SRE sent interim RCA and mitigation steps to AcmeRetail; offered dedicated support window for stabilization.

2026-03-14 18:00 UTC - Next steps: complete PR review and run a staged canary across low-risk tenants, then ramp to Dedicated pools. Finalize runbook updates and schedule post-incident retrospective with product/solutions teams.
